> Sendme transfers and restores no longer exhaust a small temp partition, long `init` phases stay visibly alive instead of looking hung, and a bare `cwcli` prints help again instead of crashing. Agents can also ask `cwcli axi url` for the address a bench actually answers on.

### New Features

* `cwcli axi url` reports the host address a bench actually answers on and checks it with a real request, naming the site it asked. Nothing else on the agent surface states that address today; the existing health check only measures the internal container port

### Bug Fixes

* A bare `cwcli` prints help again instead of crashing with a raw traceback on some installs
* Sendme transfers and restores no longer exhaust a small temp partition: both stream through cwcli's own home, copy each file once instead of twice, and report a disk-space shortage before staging or downloading a backup
* `restore --receive` validates the site and ticket before the download starts, not after
* Long `cwcli init` phases stay visibly alive instead of looking hung
* The published package no longer ships the test suite; a packaging allow-list now excludes tests and fixtures by construction
* `cwcli rm`, `cwcli restart`, `cwcli stop`, and `cwcli start` accept clustered and attached short options (`-vy`, `-pweb`) instead of refusing them
* Installing, uninstalling, updating, or checking out an app now fully resynchronizes a running bench instead of leaving stale processes serving old code
* Bench listings stop vouching for a bench that no longer exists
* A stranded migrate lock is now diagnosed with a pointer to `cwcli unlock` instead of failing opaquely
* Adding a bench to an already-running instance no longer risks restarting every other bench on it
* Bench numbers stay stable across additions instead of silently renumbering
* `cwcli init` no longer crashes on Windows during user-ID alignment

### Other Changes

* `cwcli axi` help output is concise TOON across every command, fixing truncated descriptions, leaked markdown, and inconsistent argument names
